faq: Which analytics tool do you set up?

Google Analytics 4 is the default because it is free and widely used. If you prefer Plausible, Matomo or Shopify's own reports, we can set those up instead and tell you what each one can and cannot show.
Will it work with my store platform?
Yes. We install it on Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix, Squarespace and custom sites, using the platform's own integration where it is reliable and code snippets where it is not.

Only visitors who allow it where the law requires consent. For stores serving the EU, UK or California, add the Privacy and Consent service so tracking waits for permission. Some blockers will hide a share of visits.
Do I own the analytics account?
Always. We create or use a property in your Google account and add our staff email as an editor. When the work ends you can remove us in a few clicks, and nothing is lost.

desc:
Google Analytics 4 setup for online stores gives you a working view of traffic, sales and shopper behavior. Ecom Swift LLC creates the property in your own account, installs it on your site and checks that visits and orders arrive correctly.

## What is Google Analytics 4, and why does a store need it?

Google Analytics 4 is a free tool from Google that records what visitors do on your website and groups the results into reports. For a store, it answers basic but vital questions: how many people visit, where they come from, which pages they view and how many buy.

Without it, you rely on gut feeling and platform dashboards that each tell part of the story. With a wrongly set up property, you may rely on numbers that are worse than nothing, because they look believable. A careful setup is the difference between the two.

## How good analytics changes the way you run a store

Analytics lets you see which traffic sources produce orders, not just visits. A channel that sends thousands of visitors and no sales looks very different from one that sends a few hundred buyers. You can then spend time and money where it works.

It also shows page behavior. Product pages with many views and few add to carts, landing pages that people leave straight away, and search terms visitors type with no results all become visible. Each one is a prompt for a specific improvement.

Linking Google Search Console adds the searches that bring people to your site. Campaign link naming rules keep email, social and ad traffic in separate, readable groups instead of one muddled pile.

Analytics cannot see every visitor. Browser settings, blockers and consent choices mean some activity goes unrecorded, so treat the data as a reliable guide rather than an exact count.

## What a complete setup includes

- A Google Analytics 4 property and web data stream created in your own account.
- The tracking code installed once, through your theme, your platform or Tag Manager.
- Filters that keep your own team's visits out of the reports.
- Enhanced measurement settings reviewed and set for your site.
- Ecommerce reporting for product views, add to cart, checkout and purchase.
- Key actions marked as conversions, such as purchases and sign-ups.
- Search Console linked, so search queries appear next to behavior.
- Currency, time zone and data retention settings set correctly.
- Campaign link naming rules, written down for your team.
- A setup document that records what was done and where.

## How we set up your analytics

First we check whether you already have an analytics account, and what is installed. Old Universal Analytics code or duplicate tags are common, and installing a new tag on top of them creates double counting. We tidy that before adding anything.

Then we create the property under your Google account, so you are the owner from the start. We add the data stream, install the tag in the way that suits your platform, set the filters and review the settings that decide what gets recorded.

Finally, we test. We open the site in a fresh browser, watch the visit appear in real-time reports and, for stores, place a test order and check that revenue is recorded once. We then walk you through the five reports most worth opening each week. Basic delivers a working installation. Standard adds ecommerce reporting, conversions, Search Console and naming rules. Premium covers up to three sites, shopper behavior reports, access for your team, a recorded training and a setup document.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Own the analytics account under your business email.
- Give access to staff by invitation, with the lowest role they need.
- Mark only your most important actions as conversions.
- Use consistent campaign link names.
- Open the same few reports every week.

**Avoid:**
- Letting a developer or agency own the property.
- Installing the tracking code in more than one place.
- Marking every event as a conversion.
- Looking at data from the first day and drawing conclusions.
- Leaving old analytics tags on the site after switching.

## Who analytics setup is for

It suits new store owners who are about to launch and want data from day one, and established stores that never had analytics set up well. It also helps businesses moving from an older tool or a new platform, where the previous setup did not come along.

## What we need from you

The address of your site, a Google account to own the analytics property, and access to your store or site as collaborator, staff or editor. If you use Search Console or Tag Manager, include them. We never need your passwords. Tell us who on your team should see reports, so we set the right access.
